page.layout: One printed page. Top: page number at upper left, running head "EMBLEMA" centred, then a full-width title "PRO PATRIA MORI" with subtitle "pulchrum." Centre: a woodcut emblem (armour, weapons, flag, drum and bags of coin) in a framed box. Below the woodcut: four lines of italic verse, centred. Bottom right: catchword "Omnia" with a superscript mark.

main_text.l: [woodcut emblem: weapons, flag, drum and bags; no text]

l.i: Est etiam sæuo licitum decernere bello,
Non aliter tuto viuere quando licet:
Attendas autem prudens ante omnia causam,
Quæ nisi iusta subest subtrahat arma pudor:

page.notes: The woodcut is an emblem picture with no printed words inside the frame. The running head "EMBLEMA" is set in small capitals. The number "56" is printed at upper left, in the old form with a long-s style figure. The catchword "Omnia" carries a superscript mark which may be a signature reference. The verse lines are set in italic type and the letters "Est" and "Quæ" use the long-s form, transcribed here as plain s.
